recent_posts.title: ServiceNow Knowledge 2026: Accelerating intelligent automation at scale
recent_posts.summary: Dynatrace is a Gold sponsor at ServiceNow Knowledge 2026 (May 5–7, Las Vegas), showcasing joint integrations with ServiceNow for autonomous IT operations. Key highlights include a new Now Assist and Dynatrace MCP Server integration for zero-outage outcomes, real-time digital experience context via RUM signals, enriched ITOM alerts with root cause and severity, and continued CMDB enrichment. recent_posts.title: Dynatrace Release Radar 03.26
recent_posts.summary: Dynatrace's March SaaS releases (1.334 and 1.335) bring several platform improvements: the Compliance Assistant is now generally available with real-time DORA compliance tracking; a new native vulnerability feed improves accuracy and reduces noise for security teams; Grail lookup tables are generally available, enabling business context enrichment in dashboards and DQL queries; synthetic browser monitoring gains richer execution details, a requests waterfall view, and Grail event storage; and dashboard/notebook enhancements include multi-tile resizing, time series annotations, table detail panels, and a new log usage dashboard.

recent_posts.title: Dynatrace expands AI Coding Agent monitoring for Claude Code, Google Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, OpenCode, and GitHub Copilot SDK
recent_posts.summary: Dynatrace has expanded its AI observability platform to support monitoring of multiple AI coding agents including Claude Code, Google Gemini CLI, OpenAI Codex CLI, OpenCode, and GitHub Copilot SDK. For agents that emit OpenTelemetry natively (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, OpenCode), Dynatrace can ingest telemetry on sessions, tokens, costs, tool executions, errors, and performance without code changes. GitHub Copilot SDK integration adds production context and software delivery automation. The goal is to give engineering leaders, platform teams, and developers a single observability layer to track adoption, costs, reliability, and engineering outcomes across all coding agents in use.

recent_posts.title: Observability is a team sport
recent_posts.summary: Observability should not be siloed into a single centralized team but treated as a shared responsibility across developers, SREs, QA, DevOps, and platform engineers. Developers should own code-based OpenTelemetry instrumentation since they know their applications best, while platform/SRE teams manage OTel Collector infrastructure. CI/CD pipelines also benefit from observability, with an emerging OTel CI/CD SIG providing a shared standard. Organizations should have an 'observability practices team' focused on standards, tooling governance, and cross-team advocacy rather than hands-on instrumentation or infrastructure management. Avoiding tool sprawl and operating without silos is key to effective observability at scale.

recent_posts.title: index4j: Open-source FM-Index for fast queries on compressed logs
recent_posts.summary: index4j is an open-source Java library from Dynatrace Research that implements the FM-Index data structure for fast, arbitrary substring search over compressed log data. The FM-Index combines compression and indexing into a single structure using suffix arrays, wavelet trees, and the Burrows–Wheeler transform. A practical walkthrough shows how to build an index over ~180 MB of Android logs (compressed to ~70 MB), run count and locate queries in microseconds, extract matching log lines, and serialize the index to disk. The library is available on Maven Central and suits static log datasets requiring frequent, unpredictable substring queries.

recent_posts.title: Best practices for hashing variable-length data structures
recent_posts.summary: Hashing data structures with variable-length fields is error-prone because naive string concatenation loses field boundaries, causing collisions. Three strategies are compared: delimiters (simple but fragile with special characters), length prefixes (standard in protocols like Protobuf), and length postfixes (better for streaming and nested structures). Mixing strategies is discouraged unless done carefully. Fixed-size integers are recommended for encoding lengths, while variable-length encodings like VarInt add overhead and complexity. Dynatrace's open-source Hash4j library implements the length-postfix strategy in Java, providing methods like putString, putByteArray, and putOrderedIterable that handle variable-length fields safely and support nested structures.

recent_posts.title: Unlocking a new era of digital innovation with Dynatrace and AWS
recent_posts.summary: Dynatrace is showcasing its partnership with AWS at AWS Summits, demonstrating integrations between Dynatrace's observability platform and AWS services including Amazon Bedrock, SageMaker, and the AWS DevOps Agent. Key highlights include the Clouds app for unified CloudWatch metrics visibility, Dynatrace MCP for sharing context across agent-driven systems, and support for Bedrock AgentCore at scale. The post invites attendees to visit the Dynatrace booth for live demos.

recent_posts.title: Dynatrace for AI: Teach your AI coding agent how to use Dynatrace
recent_posts.summary: Dynatrace has released 'Dynatrace for AI', an open-source collection of agent skills and prompt templates that give AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor, Cline, etc.) domain expertise to work accurately with Dynatrace. Agent skills are SKILL.md files loaded on demand without bloating context windows. The first release covers DQL query fundamentals, observability across services/traces/logs, infrastructure (Kubernetes, AWS), and dashboard creation. Prompt templates for performance regression analysis, daily standups, and incident troubleshooting are also included. Skills work alongside the Dynatrace MCP server or dtctl CLI to enable live queries. Installation is a single npx command or Claude Code plugin activation.

recent_posts.title: Google Cloud Next 2026: A look into the autonomous future of cloud operations
recent_posts.summary: At Google Cloud Next 2026, the partnership between Google Cloud and observability platform is highlighted through several announcements: a new enterprise agent available on Google Cloud marketplace, integrated autonomous incident response combining AI-driven root cause analysis with Google Cloud's telemetry, and an enhanced cloud app providing unified visibility across Google Cloud environments. The post emphasizes how AI-powered observability, automation, and agentic AI guardrails are essential for enterprises scaling AI workloads safely on cloud-native infrastructure.

recent_posts.title: What's new in Dynatrace SaaS 1.337
recent_posts.summary: Dynatrace SaaS 1.337 introduces expanded Azure cloud monitoring in the Clouds app with unified metrics, logs, topology, pre-configured health alerts, and a fully managed low-ops setup. Service Detection v2 for AWS Lambda is now in Early Access. Other highlights include record-based anomaly detection alerts, a standardized event.severity field aligned with ITIL, improved Grail DQL query metadata with bucket contribution breakdowns, OpenPipeline extraction processor recommendations, Smartscape side panel navigation, and Ownership integration with Smartscape. Several bug fixes and deprecation notices for Configuration API endpoints are also included.
